contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants from UK state schools who meet one of three flags (free school meals, a deprived neighbourhood, or a below-average school), or who are care experienced, estranged or refugees, can get an offer of up to two grades lower; completing a listed access programme can also give a reduced offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 2 A level grades lower than the standard offer (e.g. AAB rather than AAA), and/or an additional requirement such as an admissions test removed

criteria.detail: Individual Free School Meals flag: eligible for UK government-funded Free School Meals at some point in the past eight years (data comes from UCAS up to the end of Key Stage 4; for Key Stage 5 only, your school must confirm in writing).
Neighbourhood flag: lives in an area with a high level of deprivation (Index of Multiple Deprivation, 0-20%).
School flag: completed studies at schools/colleges where performance was below average and Free School Meals eligibility was higher than average.
Care experienced: a 'looked after child' for at least 3 months and eligible for Home fees (evidence needed; applicants from independent schools are also considered).
Estranged from both parents (under 25, studying without their support and approval) and eligible for Home fees (evidence needed).

UK-based, Home-fee applicants with humanitarian protection, refugee status or limited leave under the UKVI Afghan or Ukraine schemes, who studied A levels or equivalent in a UK school or college (evidence needed).

Successfully completed Realising Opportunities, Pathways to Law, Pathways to Banking and Finance or Pathways to Engineering (at Warwick or another university): considered for a reduced 'alternative' offer without meeting the flags above. Warwick Scholars Access participants are guaranteed an offer.

contextual.rulesText: State-school, Home-fee applicants who meet ONE of the three flags (free school meals, neighbourhood, school) are considered for a contextual offer. Care experienced, estranged and refugee applicants qualify without any other flag (the FAQ says independent-school applicants in these three groups are also considered). Undergraduate entry only (no foundation-year or graduate courses); eligibility does not guarantee an offer. Not currently counted: unpaid caring responsibilities, parenting responsibilities, armed forces connections, and disability or medical conditions (use the extenuating circumstances form instead). You do not have to make Warwick your firm choice.

source.evidence: applicants from UK state schools who are eligible for Home fees and meet one of the following contextual ‘flags’ will be considered for a Contextual offer

programmes.name: Warwick Scholars (access programme)
programmes.summary: Regional access programme from late Year 12 through Year 13 with 1:1 online tutoring in an A level subject, a Warwick student mentor, campus and department visits, and a residential launch event.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students with Home fee status and at least five GCSEs at grades 9-6 who attend a school/college or live in one of the Warwick-area local authorities (Coventry, Warwickshire, Birmingham, Solihull, Dudley, Sandwell, Walsall, Wolverhampton, Staffordshire, Northamptonshire, Worcestershire, Leicester, Leicestershire) and meet the widening participation criteria. Care leavers at a school or college in England can also apply.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Location: attend a school/college or live in the listed local authority areas (care leavers: a school or college in England). Academic: first year of Level 3 study, at least five GCSEs at 9-6 (4 in English Language and Maths if not among them), meet the subject requirements of the course. Prioritised if care experienced, a care leaver, or estranged from both parents; otherwise at least two of: free school meals now or in the last six years, first generation in the family to attend university, a priority school (below-average KS4 results, or bottom 40% at KS5), a priority neighbourhood (IMD 0-20%), significant extenuating circumstances.
benefits: Guaranteed offer of 2-4 grades lower than the standard entry requirements for your chosen course
50% tuition fee discount for each year of study (if you complete the programme and meet your offer)
Bursary of up to £2,000 a year towards on-campus accommodation or travel
1:1 online tutoring in one A level subject, a student mentor and an Easter revision bootcamp in Year 13

programmes.name: Pathways to Banking & Finance (at Warwick)
programmes.summary: Free two-year programme (Year 12 and 13) with finance-sector work-experience opportunities, networking, Economics and Business taster lectures, UCAS support and a summer residential national conference.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students who have always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college and live within reasonable commuting distance of Warwick; preference to those meeting one or more widening participation criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: always attended a state-funded, non-fee-paying school/college; in Year 12 at the start; live within reasonable commuting distance of Warwick. Preference to those who have about five GCSEs at 9-6 (at least two at 9-7) including Maths and English at 9-6, would be first in the family to go to university, received free school meals at secondary school, attend a school with lower-than-average progression to higher education or higher-than-average free school meals, live in a low-progression or deprived neighbourhood, or have been looked after, in care or a young carer. The more criteria you meet, the more likely you are to be offered a place.
benefits: Completers (at any Pathways university) are eligible for a reduced offer at Warwick, up to 2 A level grades lower
Chance to join the Warwick Scholars undergraduate programme once you enrol
Work-experience opportunities, finance networking, Economics and Business taster lectures
programmes.offerReduction: Up to 2 A level grades lower than the standard offer (alternative offer, not guaranteed; in most cases the same as the contextual offer)
programmes.subjects: Banking, finance, Economics and Business (separate Law and Engineering streams also run)

programmes.name: mA*ths Online Programme (at Warwick)
programmes.summary: Year 12 and Year 13 support for A level Maths students considering a maths-related degree: masterclass days on campus, two seven-week online courses and online mentoring from Warwick students.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students taking at least three A levels including Maths, with at least a 6 in GCSE Maths and Science, who are capable of an A in A level Maths and plan to apply for courses with a large maths component; priority to students from under-represented groups. Warwick's places mainly go to the West Midlands and Northamptonshire; students from regions without a hub may apply to a university they can practically travel to.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Priority to applicants meeting at least one of: free school meals, priority neighbourhood (IMD 0-20%), care experienced or care leaver, estranged from both parents. Additional criteria: refugee or asylum seeker, caring responsibilities, armed forces family, first in family to go to university, household income below £50,000 a year, school with below-average attainment or a high percentage of free school meals. Must be willing and able to travel to Warwick up to twice a year on weekend dates.
benefits: Introductory and closing masterclass days at Warwick with academics, MEI and student mentors
Two seven-week online courses fitted to the A level Maths curriculum
Ongoing online mentoring from current Warwick students
